upstream.observed_formula: MEM_BEFORE and MEM_AFTER are VmRSS samples from /proc/$$/status of the wrapper shell; memory.peak is max(MEM_BEFORE, MEM_AFTER), not a sampled child-command peak.

hypothesis_under_test: bash_wrapper_local.sh memory.peak is a valid measurement of child tool-call peak memory.

counterexample.environment: isolated local deterministic Linux container; donor falsifier only
counterexample.experiment_spec: Parent shell records its own VmRSS before/after. A child Python process touches a 192 MiB bytearray, records its own VmRSS while allocation is live, then exits. Apply the audited local-wrapper max(parent_before,parent_after) formula.

result.finding: The no-root local wrapper's peak field measures endpoint RSS of the wrapper process, not the child command's true peak. A short-lived high-memory child can be missed by roughly two orders of magnitude in this controlled example.
result.scope_note: The numeric ratio is environment/example-specific. The reproduced structural failure is that the formula cannot observe a child's transient peak because it samples the parent only before and after child execution.

f2_architecture_delta.recommended_rule: Never label parent endpoint RSS as child/effect peak memory. Resource receipts must bind measurement provenance and metric semantics; child peak requires a measurement source that actually covers the child execution interval, such as admitted cgroup memory.peak or an equivalent verified observer.
f2_architecture_delta.authority_boundary: A fallback estimator must be explicitly typed ESTIMATE/DEGRADED, never silently upgraded to OBSERVED_CHILD_PEAK.

counterhypothesis_remaining: A portable non-cgroup sampler could estimate child peaks sufficiently well if it follows the child/process tree at adequate sampling frequency and quantifies missed-burst error; that mechanism was not tested here.
